questions.question:
Which of the following statement is correct regarding inertia?

I. Inertia is the natural tendency of an object to resist a change in its state of motion or of rest.

II. The mass of an object is a measure of its inertia.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Both I and II **__ [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Newton's first law of motion** 

 
 
• **States that "An object at rest stays at rest and an object in motion stays in motion with the same speed and in the same direction unless acted upon by an unbalanced force."**
 
• Objects tend to "keep on doing what they're doing."
 
• In fact, it is the natural tendency of objects to resist changes in their state of motion.
 
• **This tendency to resist changes in their state of motion is described as inertia.**
 
 

**​(Hence statement I is correct)**

 
• **Inertia:**

 
 
• The resistance an object has to a change in its state of motion.
 
• All objects resist changes in their state of motion. All objects have this tendency - they have inertia.
 
• **The tendency of an object to resist changes in its state of motion varies with mass.**
 
 

**​((Hence statement II is correct))**

 
• Mass is that quantity that is solely dependent upon the inertia of an object.
 
• The more inertia that an object has, the more mass that it has.
 
• A more massive object has a greater tendency to resist changes in its state of motion.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Laws of motion:**

 
 

 **Law of Motion**
 **Description**
 **Example**
 
 
 
 

 Newton's First Law
 An object at rest tends to stay at rest, and an object in motion tends to stay in motion with the same speed and direction unless acted upon by an external force.
 A book resting on a table will remain at rest until an external force, such as pushing it, is applied.
 
 

 Newton's Second Law
 The acceleration of an object is directly proportional to the net force acting on it and inversely proportional to its mass.
 If you push a small ball and a large ball with the same amount of force, the smaller ball will experience a larger acceleration due to its lower mass.
 
 

 Newton's Third Law
 For every action, there is an equal and opposite reaction.
 When you swim, the action of pushing the water backwards with your arms and legs creates an equal and opposite reaction that propels you forward.

questions.question:
Macroeconomics deals with which of the following studies?

I. Reasons behind the unemployment of resources

II. Determination of total output
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Both I and II.**__ [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• Macroeconomics is a branch of economics that deals with the structure, **performance, and behaviour of the overall economy.**
 
• It focuses on areas like **inflation, economic growth rate, price levels of various goods and services, gross domestic product (GDP), national income and the unemployment rate in a particular country.**
 
• The study of macroeconomics is essential to understand the economic performance of a nation and the factors that affect it.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

__
 
• **Macroeconomics deals with the following studies:**
 
• **Reasons behind the unemployment of resources: **
 
 
• Macroeconomics focuses on understanding and analyzing the factors that contribute to unemployment on a broader scale.
 
• It examines the causes and consequences of unemployment, such as changes in aggregate **demand, labour market conditions, technological advancements, and government policies that affect employment levels.**
 
 
 
• **Determination of total output: **
 
 
• Macroeconomics is concerned with studying and explaining the determinants of a country's** total output or national income. **
 
• **I**t analyzes the factors that **influence aggregate production and economic growth, including consumption, investment, government spending, and net exports**.
 
• Macroeconomists investigate the relationship between these variables and their impact on **overall economic performance**.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• The Citizenship Act was first passed in India in the year **1955.**
 
• **The original Citizenship Act of 1955 **laid down the framework for Indian citizenship and defined the various ways in which a person could acquire or lose citizenship in India.
 
• Since its enactment, the act has undergone several amendments to accommodate changes and evolving perspectives on citizenship. 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• There are four main ways through which an individual can acquire Indian citizenship:
 
 
• **By Birth:** A person born in India on or after January 26, 1950, is considered an Indian citizen by birth, with a few exceptions.
 
• **By Descent:** Individuals born outside India on or after January 26, 1950, but have at least one Indian parent, are eligible for Indian citizenship by descent.
 
• **By Registration: **Certain categories of people, such as individuals of Indian origin residing outside India, can acquire Indian citizenship through registration by fulfilling specific criteria.
 
• **By Naturalization:** Foreigners who have resided in India for a specified period of time and meet other qualifications can apply for Indian citizenship through naturalization.

questions.question: ______ is an Act of the Parliament of the United Kingdom that partitioned British India into two new independent dominions of India and Pakistan in 1947.

__
 
• **The Indian Independence Act of 1947** partitioned British India into two separate dominions, **India and Pakistan, based on religious lines.**
 
• The act facilitated the transfer of power from British colonial rule to the newly formed governments of **India and Pakistan.**
 
• It granted full **legislative authority to India and Pakistan**, establishing them as independent and sovereign nations.
 
• The partition resulted in widespread communal violence and riots between religious communities, leading to a significant loss of life and displacement of people.
 
• The act allowed princely states to choose between joining India, joining Pakistan, or remaining independent, leaving the decision to the rulers of these states.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **The Rowlatt Act**, also known as the Anarchical and Revolutionary** Crimes Act of 1919,** was a legislative act passed by the British colonial government in India during the period of British rule.

 
 
• It was named after its sponsor,** Sir Sidney Rowlatt,** who was a British judge.
 
 
 
• **The Government of India Act** refers to several legislative acts passed by the** British Parliament** during the period of **British rule in India.**
 
 
• These acts were intended to regulate and govern the administration of **British India.**
 
 
 
• **​Pitt's India Act, **officially known as the** East India Company Act 1784**, was an important piece of legislation passed by the **British Parliament under the leadership of Prime Minister William Pitt the Younger.**
 
 
• The act was designed to bring about significant reforms in the governance and administration of the British East India Company's territories in India.
